newsitem.title: UK: Britain "arms for oil" deal with Argentina - paper.
newsitem.headline: Britain "arms for oil" deal with Argentina - paper.

text.p: Britain has agreed to a secret plan to re-equip the Argentine navy, its foe in the 1982 Falklands War, in return for a deal to explore for oil around the islands in the south Atlantic, a newspaper said on Sunday.

"Ministers do not intend to reveal the intended relaxation of its weapons embargo against Argentina, despite the controversy sparked by a similar move in the "arms to Iraq' affair," The Observer said.
It says Britain is keeping the plan under wraps because it is concerned it could incite public rage in the run-up to a general election which must be called by May 1997.
The proposed deal would allow Rolls-Royce to open negotiations to export key components to the Argentine navy which will enable it to repair engines in six of its major warships.
In exchange Argentina would approve a three-way deal to give British companies access to the potential oil-bonanzas in the South Atlantic. Exploration licences will be awarded on October 28.
A spokesman for Britain's Department of Trade and Industry said he had no information about a change in policy.
"The embargo is in place," he told Reuters. "Its existence and policy on its applications on defence sales is kept under regular review," he added.

Relations between Britain and Argentina have been strained since the Falklands War 14 years ago. About 1,000 servicemen, three-quarters of them Argentine, died after Britain sent a task force to Argentina to end a brief Argentine occupation of the islands.
The two countries restored diplomatic relations in 1989, but Buenos Aires still claims sovereignty over the sparsely populated Falklands which are known in Argentina as Malvinas.
A representative of the Falklands Island government in London told The Observer that a change in the embargo would cause worry.
"Any relaxation of the embargo would be of concern. Argentina is still seen as a threat," Sukie Cameron told the newspaper.
